rule_metadata.description: The definitive, centralized module for Madd Tamkeen, covering both double-Ya and Waw-to-Waw letter empowerment to preserve crisp individual articulation and prevent accidental merging.

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Tamkeen (تَمْكِين) means establishment, empowerment, or providing firm phonetic footing.
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: Madd Tamkeen occurs when two identical or closely related weak letters meet—specifically requiring a 2-count separation so neither letter is swallowed, compressed, or merged away.

comprehensive_sub_types.type_one_double_ya: Ya Saakinah (or weak Ya) preceded by a vowelled Ya carrying a Shaddah (e.g., عِلِّيِّينَ, النَّبِيِّينَ). The first Ya is stressed and vowelled, while the second Ya is Saakin, empowered with a 2-count duration.
comprehensive_sub_types.type_two_waw_and_ya_separation: Waw Madd meeting a vowelled Waw (or Ya Madd meeting a vowelled Ya) across words or within words to ensure distinct individual articulation without slurring.

theoretical_foundation.ruling_and_duration: Fixed lengthening of exactly **2 counts** (Harakat) across all authentic transmission paths.
theoretical_foundation.mushaf_indicator: Explicit double-letter combinations where one is vowelled/stressed and the other acts as a Madd/Saakin letter.

practical_examples.breakdown: Stressed Ya with Shaddah and Kasrah followed by Ya Saakinah; empowered with 2 counts.
Empowerment lengthening between double Ya combination.
Waw Madd meeting succeeding vowelled Waw in connective phrasing requiring Tamkeen separation.
